subject: history_social
passage: Hampi, in the Indian state of Karnataka, was once the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, which controlled much of southern India from the fourteenth to the sixteenth century. Among its most photographed monuments is a stone chariot in the courtyard of the Vittala Temple. The ______ which was built in the sixteenth century and whose carved stone wheels were once said to turn on their axles, is actually a shrine dedicated to Garuda, the eagle who carries the god Vishnu.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The clause "which was built in the sixteenth century and whose carved stone wheels were once said to turn on their axles" is extra information about the chariot. It closes with a comma before the verb "is," so it must open with a comma after "chariot."
explanation.A: Correct. The comma opens the pair of commas around the nonessential clause, matching the comma before "is."
explanation.B: Incorrect. A semicolon can't separate the subject "The chariot" from the rest of its own clause.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Extra information must be set off by matching marks; a dash can't open a clause that closes with a comma.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Without an opening comma, the clause is not set off, and the comma before "is" separates the subject from its verb.
